description.from:
**Follow-on under `PPY-54055d`.** Diagnose already fuses heuristics, profile `rules:`, and 4-gram redundancy. This slice adds **conventional** density signals — not neural sentence embeddings.

## Intent

As a publication operator, I want diagnose to flag long, low-content drafts using measures other people already use for “how much is said per word,” so fluff is a steer-able finding without inventing a new metric family.

## Conventional signals (golden path)

Do **not** add local MiniLM/fastembed/ONNX sentence embeddings. That is a paraphrase-clustering technique, not a named information-density measure, and it is out of this story.

Use the usual mix:

1. **Lexical density** (Ure/Halliday): content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs) / total words. Low density = function-word padding.
2. **Compression ratio**: `gzip` length / raw length. Highly compressible drafts are repetitive or formulaic.
3. **Existing 4-gram redundancy** (already in diagnose). Unchanged.

These are independent red flags plus one `density` summary. No weighted fluff score. Not an AI-detector (no surprisal, perplexity, burstiness, UID).

**Honest limit:** three paraphrases of one claim in different words will usually **not** fire these. Verbatim/near-copy stays on 4-grams. Semantic restatement is out of scope here.

## Done when

- `checks.informationDensity` (default on) and optional `density:` thresholds: `minWords`, `minLexicalDensity` (flag when density is below this), `maxGzipRatio` (flag when gzip size/raw size is below this — more compressible). Names must match the inequalities in code and Gherkin.
- Diagnose JSON includes `density`: `wordCount`, `sentenceCount`, `lexicalDensity`, `gzipRatio`. No `embedder`, no vector model id, no API vendor.
- Long synthetic fluff (high function-word rate and/or high compressibility) produces `low_information_density` when `wordCount >= minWords`.
- A must-pass Anth.us reference excerpt above `minWords` does not.
- Short drafts below `minWords` do not get the document-level flag.
- Content-word heuristic is deterministic (POS via a small closed-class function-word list, or equivalent stdlib approach). No spaCy/GPU/model download required in CI.
- Detector-score keys remain forbidden.

## Out of scope

- Sentence embeddings, fastembed, sentence-transformers, OpenAI/remote embeddings, TF-IDF sentence clustering as a “concept count.”
- Propositional idea density / CPIDR (heavier parser; later if we want the Nun-Study measure).
- Rewrite options (PPY-73906c), verifier (PPY-5ca22f), Newsroom UI.

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: Diagnose information density from conventional signals
  As a publication operator
  I want lexical density and compression in diagnose JSON
  So long padded drafts are a steer-able red flag without a custom embedding pipeline

  Scenario: Density summary is present
    Given a loadable style profile with information density enabled
    And a draft of several sentences
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then the JSON includes density with wordCount, sentenceCount, lexicalDensity, and gzipRatio
    And the JSON does not include an embedder field

  Scenario: Long low-content fluff is flagged
    Given a draft longer than the profile minWords that is padded with function words and repeats
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is a low_information_density finding

  Scenario: House-voice excerpt is not flagged as fluff
    Given a must-pass excerpt from an Anth.us reference sample longer than minWords
    And the Anth.us style profile
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no low_information_density finding

  Scenario: Short drafts skip the document-level density flag
    Given a draft shorter than the profile minWords
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no low_information_density finding
```
description.to:
**Follow-on under `PPY-54055d`.** Diagnose already fuses heuristics, profile `rules:`, and 4-gram shingles. This slice adds the **usual NLP use of sentence embeddings**: cluster near-paraphrases so restated claims are steer-able findings.

## Intent

As a publication operator, I want diagnose to flag sentences that say the same thing in different words the way summarization and duplicate-detection pipelines already do — local sentence embeddings + cosine clusters — not a homemade “information density” or “concept count” score.

## Golden path (what this is)

Sentence-embedding similarity for **paraphrase / redundant sentence** groups. Same family as STS, MMR, and extractive-summarization duplicate dropping. Local model only (ONNX MiniLM-class or equivalent). No paid vector API. Do not call OpenAI or `papyrus_knowledge_query` embeddings.

**Not in this story:** lexical density, gzip-as-density, propositional idea density, Uniform Information Density, a document-level fluff score, or “cluster count = number of concepts.”

## Fusion

Independent findings, as today. A `concept_restatement` group (same shape as 4-gram `repetition_groups`) when a similarity cluster has enough sentences that are **not** already explained by 4-gram redundancy. The operator/LLM steers those groups (rewrite/delete). Diagnose still does not rewrite.

Optional tiny `similarity` summary for debugging (sentenceCount, clusterCount, embedder id) is fine; it is not a score to game and must not be named information density.

## Done when

- `checks.semanticRestatement` (default on) and optional `similarity:` thresholds: `cosineThreshold`, `restatementMinSentences`, `embedder`: `local` | `off`.
- Local embedder is optional at install (Poetry extra). If missing, this check is a no-op (no groups, or explicit skip) — do **not** silently invent a TF-IDF “concept density” substitute. Tests inject vectors so CI does not download a model.
- A fixture that restates one claim three times in different wording (no shared 4-gram) produces a `concept_restatement` group when embeddings are injected or the local model is present.
- 4-gram redundancy still catches verbatim repeats; semantic groups must not duplicate those spans.
- Detector-score keys remain forbidden.

## Out of scope

Lexical density / gzip density (rejected as the replacement for embeddings). Rewrite options (PPY-73906c). Verifier (PPY-5ca22f). Newsroom UI.

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: Semantic restatement via local sentence embeddings
  As a publication operator
  I want paraphrase clusters in diagnose JSON
  So I can steer repeated claims that 4-gram shingles miss

  Scenario: Three paraphrases of one claim are clustered
    Given a draft that states the same claim three times in different words with no repeated four-word phrase
    And a loadable style profile with semantic restatement enabled
    When I run the diagnose command with an injected embedder that places those sentences in one cluster
    Then there is a concept_restatement group with at least three member sentences
    And that group is not justified only by four-word shingles

  Scenario: Verbatim repeats stay on existing redundancy
    Given a draft that repeats the same four-word phrase in two sentences
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then those sentences are a redundancy group
    And they are not also a concept_restatement group

  Scenario: Check can be disabled
    Given a style profile with semantic restatement disabled
    And a paraphrase draft
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no concept_restatement group
```
